candidates.title: SPH external readout of the PTB-XL heads (022)
candidates.question: How much of the development AUROC survives on an unseen hospital with human labels?
candidates.evidence: All our numbers are single-source PTB-XL development. Leinonen et al. (arXiv:2403.15012, Tables 4-5): K-fold estimates overstate new-source AUROC by 0.04-0.13; a ResNet identifies the source from ECG, age and sex with 96.9% accuracy.
candidates.notes: Done 28 September 2026: SPH AUROC CPC 0.876, JEPA 0.911, xECG 0.915; docs/experiment-022-sph-external-readout-results.md. Measured about 3.5 h build (subagent) and 0.3 h GPU.

candidates.title: EchoNext structural heart disease readout (023)
candidates.question: Do our frozen features detect echo-confirmed structural heart disease, the only label that is a cardiopathy rather than an ECG annotation?
candidates.evidence: Benchmark (arXiv:2509.25095, Table 3): ECG-CPC ranks first on EchoNext (0.831 fine-tuned); section 4.4: JEPA best below 1,000 labels, CPC higher ceiling. HuBERT-ECG v4: macro AUROC 0.793.
candidates.notes: Done 28 September 2026 (v3): composite SHD AUROC cpc 0.812, jepa 0.823, xecg 0.838, cart tabular 0.737; cpc minus tabular +0.075 [+0.063, +0.086]; docs/experiment-023-echonext-readout-results.md.

candidates.title: Full-development standard-label rescoring of JEPA, xECG and released ECG-CPC
candidates.question: Do the hard ECGs that put CPC at chance (020) also defeat the stronger frozen encoders?
candidates.evidence: Experiment 020: CPC AUROC 0.506 on the 266 ECGs the project label dropped; all earlier encoder rankings used the project label.
candidates.notes: Done inside Experiment 022 v3: added development ECGs AUROC CPC 0.575, JEPA 0.734, xECG 0.726.

candidates.title: Label-efficiency curves of frozen JEPA, xECG and CPC at 100-2,000 labels
candidates.question: Which frozen encoder should a small university labeled set use?
candidates.evidence: Benchmark Table 31: label efficiency ratio 0.11-0.42 for ECG-JEPA, 0.21-0.40 for ECG-CPC at 250-1,000 labels. ECG-JEPA Table 3 (1% and 10% probes).
candidates.notes: Done 28 September 2026 as Experiment 025: JEPA and xECG beat CPC at every budget and with 100 labels exceed CPC at all labels; docs/experiment-025-label-efficiency-results.md. 1,430 s CPU.

candidates.title: CPC embedding geometry audit and diagnosis prototypes (024)
candidates.question: Is the embedding space organized by diagnosis or by device and demographics, and do reference vectors work?
candidates.evidence: ECG-JEPA appendix A.3 (nearest class mean) and appendix E (outliers as label errors); benchmark section 4.3 (linear versus attention head); 020 device probe AUROC 0.974.
candidates.notes: Done 28 September 2026: CPC prototype minus probe -0.077 [-0.095, -0.060]; JEPA -0.031, xECG -0.034; clusters follow device and heart rate more than diagnosis; 192 label-audit candidates; docs/experiment-024-embedding-geometry-results.md. 746 s CPU.

candidates.title: Multi-label auxiliary head on frozen features versus the binary head
candidates.question: Does training the readout on all SCP statements improve the binary endpoint?
candidates.evidence: HuBERT-ECG v4 (multitask fine-tuning on 164 harmonized labels improved low-prevalence targets without new ECGs). ProtoECGNet trains on all 71 PTB-XL labels.
candidates.notes: Cheap on cached features: e.g. a shared low-rank projection fitted on 71 labels, then the binary probe on top.

candidates.title: Device-controlled probes (drop or balance CS100 3)
candidates.question: How much of the binary AUROC depends on the recording device?
candidates.evidence: 020: CS100 3 is 35% of training folds, 74% positive, and identifiable at AUROC 0.974.
candidates.notes: Cached features; compare per-device development AUROC. Value lowered 29 September 2026: 024b found JEPA and xECG clusters follow diagnosis, not device or hospital; the device effect was CPC-specific.

candidates.title: Attention-pooling frozen head on encoder tokens (CPC, released ECG-CPC, xECG)
candidates.question: Is the CPC gap to JEPA and xECG a readout problem rather than a representation problem?
candidates.evidence: Benchmark Tables 4-5: ECG-CPC PTB-XL super 0.863 linear versus 0.919 with a query-attention head; section 4.3 attributes it to the token-level objective. Our local readout: +0.0125 AUROC from token maxima.
candidates.notes: Frozen encoder, trains only a query vector and a linear layer. After 022/025 the CPC gap to JEPA/xECG is about 0.035-0.04 on both PTB-XL and SPH; this tests whether a better readout closes it.

candidates.title: Supervised S4 from scratch at matched labels (100 Hz, 2.5 s crops)
candidates.question: At 15k labels, does any self-supervised encoder beat a strong supervised baseline?
candidates.evidence: Benchmark section 4.1 and Table 34: supervised S4 reaches 0.941 on PTB-XL all, level with the best foundation models; our supervised CNN reached 0.923.
candidates.notes: Needs an S4 layer; the benchmark repository has one.

candidates.title: 2.5 s crops with test-time averaging for frozen readouts
candidates.question: Does averaging four 2.5 s windows beat one 10 s pass?
candidates.evidence: Benchmark section 3.3 and discussion: 2.5 s crops with averaging outperform full 10 s inputs.
candidates.notes: Could be an extra arm of attention_readout.

candidates.title: 017 morphology-template second-seed replication
candidates.question: Does the limited-label template gain replicate?
candidates.evidence: 017 v2 passed its limited-label screen at +0.0026 AUROC, one seed.
candidates.notes: Existing follow-up in docs/experiment-queue.json.

candidates.title: Ningbo EDA and clean manifest
candidates.question: How many Ningbo ECGs are usable, and do they overlap Chapman?
candidates.evidence: Smoke test: the first three records each had a constant lead.
candidates.notes: Module ecg_experiment/eda/ningbo.py ready. Include the exact-hash join of Ningbo against Chapman, the union, the clean cohorts and the PTB-XL held-out folds, with a receipt (cleaning review R1).

candidates.title: Quality-first nested cohorts 25k-200k
candidates.question: Build the pretraining cohorts from human-read sources first.
candidates.evidence: User decision, 28 September 2026. ECG-JEPA Table 8: adding MIMIC (180k to 960k) slightly lowered linear-probe AUROC.
candidates.notes: Script supports 150k and 200k; build only 25k-100k here.

candidates.title: Multi-source probe with leave-source-out evaluation
candidates.question: Does training the readout on PTB-XL, Chapman, Ningbo, Georgia and CPSC generalize better to a new hospital?
candidates.evidence: Leinonen et al. Table 5: leave-source-out estimates are nearly unbiased (mean error -0.006 to 0.004) where pooled K-fold is optimistic by 0.04-0.11.
candidates.notes: Done 29 September 2026 as Experiment 022b (docs/experiment-022b-multisource-readout-results.md), on the frozen Challenge record split v1 with the training quality policy. The readout fitted on PTB-XL plus 22,494 Challenge training ECGs is adopted: SPH AUROC xECG 0.915 to 0.939 (+0.024 [+0.021, +0.026]), JEPA 0.911 to 0.934, CPC 0.876 to 0.897. Leaving one family out still beats PTB-XL alone on that held-out family (+0.008 to +0.026 AUROC, 8 of 9 intervals above 0). No pooled threshold transfers to SPH; PTB-XL development falls 0.013 (xECG), mostly on the hard cases. Challenge test groups still closed. Measured with ningbo_sph_transfer.

candidates.title: Learned prototype head anchored to real training ECGs
candidates.question: Can case-based prototypes match the probe while giving a reference ECG per condition?
candidates.evidence: ProtoECGNet (MLHC 2025, Tables 1-2): 0.913 versus 0.925 black-box macro AUROC on 71 PTB-XL labels; clinicians rated prototypes representative.
candidates.notes: 024: raw CPC prototypes trail the probe by 0.077, JEPA/xECG by about 0.03, so a learned projection is needed; build it on frozen JEPA or xECG features, anchored to real training ECGs.

candidates.title: Source-controlled clustering of multi-source embeddings
candidates.question: Are there diagnosis-enriched clusters that span several hospitals?
candidates.evidence: Earlier HDBSCAN found only normal versus abnormal regions; sources are highly identifiable.
candidates.notes: 024: k-means clusters align with device (AMI 0.22-0.23) and heart rate more than diagnosis (0.06-0.09); only worth doing on a supervised projection with device and heart-rate controls. 024b ran the source-AMI step: pooled k-means clusters follow the label more than the hospital, but no cluster is a pure diagnosis.

candidates.title: CoRe-style lead-drop masking in CPC pretraining
candidates.question: Does breaking inter-lead linear shortcuts improve CPC features?
candidates.evidence: CoRe-ECG (arXiv:2604.11359, Table 5): STDM +1.4 AUROC points on PTB-XL under its own random patient split; no code.

candidates.title: ECG-report alignment with PTB-XL cardiologist reports
candidates.question: Do text-derived prototypes classify without labels?
candidates.evidence: MERL (ICML 2024) reports large gains, but its own self-supervised baselines are weak (PTB-XL super linear 0.71-0.81); in the independent benchmark MERL is mid-ranked. MERL and DiffuSETS use MIMIC machine reports, which we do not trust.
candidates.notes: Only about 21.8k German reports; check validated_by_human.

candidates.title: Beat-synchronous tokens
candidates.question: Do heartbeat-aligned tokens help?
candidates.evidence: Sameh et al. (arXiv:2608.30367, Table 1): +0.004 macro AUROC over fixed 50-sample patches; our Experiment 006 found no benefit from heartbeat chunks.
candidates.notes: Already tested in 006; the paper's effect is within our usual noise.

candidates.title: Synthetic or textbook ECGs as class reference vectors
candidates.question: Can generated or digitized ECGs serve as per-condition references?
candidates.evidence: SSSD-ECG (arXiv:2301.08227, Table I): a classifier trained only on synthetic PTB-XL ECGs scores 0.840 versus 0.932 on real, with the generator trained on PTB-XL itself. Textbook images are further out of distribution.
candidates.notes: Data-derived prototypes and medoids (024) answer the same need.

candidates.title: Apply the Challenge SNOMED equivalence pairs in the EDA
candidates.question: Are Challenge condition counts correct?
candidates.evidence: Cleaning review R2: cross.py:87-89 lists only 164909002 for LBBB; 76 of the first 95 Ningbo LBBB headers use 733534002. ISIBrno and ECG-FM read the pairs from weights.csv.
candidates.notes: Done 28 September 2026 (PR #5); no cached source used 733534002, so no count changed.

candidates.title: SNOMED-to-endpoint mapping for Challenge sources
candidates.question: Can Chapman, Ningbo, Georgia and CPSC supply the binary label?
candidates.evidence: Cleaning review R2 and R7: unscored codes must stay unresolved, and 'normal' needs an explicit rule because the Challenge NSR code is a rhythm.
candidates.notes: Needed before multisource_lso.

candidates.title: Near-duplicate pass across Challenge sources
candidates.question: Are there rescaled or shifted copies that the exact hash misses?
candidates.evidence: Cleaning review R1: no published pipeline deduplicates Chapman and Ningbo; HuBERT-ECG's shipped splits leak Chapman records.
candidates.notes: Lead II at 50 Hz, z-scored, max cross-correlation over +/-1 s within age/sex/source blocks; flag at >= 0.99 for review, do not exclude.

candidates.title: Quality policy v2 review flags (edge zero runs, short dropouts)
candidates.question: Do short zero paddings or dropouts slip through the 1 s flat-segment rule?
candidates.evidence: Cleaning review R3: JEPA and xECG check record edges for zero padding; our flat_segment needs 1 s.
candidates.notes: Versioned clean_*_v2; never edit v1. Do not adopt +/-3 mV clipping.

candidates.title: Versioned full-record resampler
candidates.question: Remove the 5 s join that historical_resample leaves for full-sequence models.
candidates.evidence: Cleaning review R4: cpc_input_audit.py:40-41 and code15_cpc.py:80 resample 5 s halves separately.
candidates.notes: Done 29 September 2026: resample_full(signal, up, down) in ecg_experiment/resample.py, one resample_poly pass per record, float32; tests/test_resample.py; docs/data-quality-assessment.md. New manifests only; frozen experiments keep historical_resample, resample_halves and to_cpc.

candidates.title: Key-checked waveform/metadata joins in every builder
candidates.question: Could any builder pair a waveform with the wrong row?
candidates.evidence: Cleaning review R8: ECG-FM, MERL and the benchmark join by position; UTU overwrites SPH IDs. EchoNext is positional by release design; our builder checks counts.
candidates.notes: Done 29 September 2026: audited all 17 scripts/data builders and their loaders. Every waveform/metadata pairing is by ID, by a per-row signal_sha256 re-check, or by an ID array or asserted ID sequence written with the waveforms; no assertion needed adding. EchoNext stays positional by release design (contiguous-split and count checks, row column re-checked by consumers); its builder and eda/echonext.py are hashed in echonext_250hz_v1/metadata.json, so they were left unchanged.

candidates.title: Zero-phase 0.5 Hz high-pass as a harmonization arm
candidates.question: Does a shared high-pass shrink the device gap and the SPH/EchoNext shift without losing development AUROC?
candidates.evidence: Cleaning review R5: SPH and EchoNext have 20-35x less power below 0.7 Hz than PTB-XL; CS100 3 is a device shortcut. Repositories disagree (none, 0.5, 0.67, 1 Hz).
candidates.notes: Filter the full record before cropping; frozen encoder, refit probes; report per device and external.

candidates.title: One-class screening: distance from the normal-ECG manifold
candidates.question: Can a model trained only on NORM ECGs flag abnormal ones, including conditions absent from our labels?
candidates.evidence: The university population is mostly healthy and rare cardiopathies have few labels; one-class density scoring needs no abnormal examples.
candidates.notes: Done 28 September 2026 as Experiment 026: Mahalanobis distance from normal, xECG 0.923 and JEPA 0.910 on development (no abnormal labels), SPH 0.858 and 0.836; matches probes trained without a held-out condition; docs/experiment-026-normal-manifold-results.md.

candidates.title: ECG heart age: predicted minus real age as a risk signal
candidates.question: Is an 'older-looking' ECG enriched for abnormal annotations or echo-confirmed disease, especially in young people?
candidates.evidence: Benchmark: frozen encoders predict age (MIMIC Age task); for a student population an age gap could flag hearts that look older than they are.
candidates.notes: Ridge on cached features, age gap versus labels; EchoNext needs its features first.

candidates.title: Vectorcardiogram features: spatial QRS-T angle and loop shape
candidates.question: Do classic dipole features from the Kors transform add to deep features for structural disease?
candidates.evidence: Spatial QRS-T angle is a known clinical marker of structural heart disease; it is derivable from 12 leads without training.
candidates.notes: Kors matrix, fiducials from a delineator; test alone and with the probe on PTB-XL and EchoNext val.

candidates.title: Device-adversarial readout (gradient reversal against source)
candidates.question: Can we remove device/source information from the features and generalize better to SPH?
candidates.evidence: 020: device probe AUROC 0.974; Leinonen et al.: source identifiable at 96.9% accuracy.
candidates.notes: Judge only on external data. 022 shows rankings survive SPH; value unchanged.

candidates.title: Heart-axis rotation augmentation via VCG projection
candidates.question: Does training invariance to simulated electrode/axis rotation reduce device and body-habitus shortcuts?
candidates.evidence: Physically grounded augmentation: project to VCG, rotate the dipole, project back to 12 leads.
candidates.notes: Pretraining study; only after the cheap readout questions are settled.

candidates.title: Frozen general time-series or audio foundation models as ECG encoders
candidates.question: Do non-ECG pretrained models (time-series or speech) carry useful ECG structure?
candidates.evidence: TiViT (important-papers.md section 36) shows vision weights transfer to time series; untested for 12-lead ECG here.
candidates.notes: Random-weight control is mandatory.

candidates.title: LLM reading PTB-XL measurements as text
candidates.question: How far does a general LLM get from interval/axis measurements alone, zero-shot?
candidates.evidence: Medical knowledge in LLMs versus learned features; a sanity baseline for interpretability.
candidates.notes: PTB-XL (public) only. Never send EchoNext, MIMIC or other credentialed data to an external API.

candidates.title: Cardiologist review of the 024 reference ECGs and label-audit list
candidates.question: Are the reference ECGs typical, and are the 20 suspect PTB-XL labels wrong?
candidates.evidence: 024 produced docs/experiment-024-clinician-review.md (public PTB-XL data).
candidates.notes: About 30-60 minutes of a cardiologist's time; record answers next to the sheet.

candidates.title: Calibrated 95%-sensitivity threshold for JEPA/xECG, checked on SPH
candidates.question: At the project's screening operating point, what specificity and false-referral rate do JEPA and xECG give at a new hospital?
candidates.evidence: 022 reports AUROC only; the project's decision rule is at least 95% sensitivity on the calibration patients, and AUROC hides false referrals.
candidates.notes: Done 28 September 2026 as Experiment 027: the PTB-XL 95% threshold does not transfer; SPH sensitivity CPC 0.971 (specificity 0.303), JEPA 0.916 (0.663), xECG 0.922 (0.646); probabilities too high at SPH; docs/experiment-027-calibrated-threshold-results.md. 692 s.

candidates.title: Concatenated ECG-JEPA and xECG features
candidates.question: Do the two strongest encoders carry complementary information?
candidates.evidence: 025: JEPA and xECG are indistinguishable on average, but come from different objectives and data (JEPA 250 Hz transformer, xECG 100 Hz xLSTM).
candidates.notes: Cached features; development and SPH (022 features) with the fixed readout. Experiment 014's JEPA+CPC fusion was negative, which lowers expectations.

candidates.title: Error analysis of the PTB-XL hard cases
candidates.question: Which statements make the ECGs the project label dropped hard even for JEPA and xECG (added-development AUROC about 0.73)?
candidates.evidence: 022 v3: added development ECGs AUROC CPC 0.575, JEPA 0.734, xECG 0.726, with 41 positives.
candidates.notes: Descriptive: false positives and negatives by SCP code, device and heart rate; training-set analogue to avoid over-reading 41 development positives.

candidates.title: Probe sensitivity to the 024 label-audit candidates
candidates.question: Does removing or down-weighting the 192 suspect training labels change development and SPH AUROC?
candidates.evidence: 024 flagged 192 training ECGs whose labels disagree with at least 80% of neighbours in both CPC and JEPA space.
candidates.notes: Better after a cardiologist has checked the top 20; otherwise it tests the neighbour rule, not label errors.

candidates.title: How many local labeled ECGs restore the 95% operating point at a new site
candidates.question: If a new site (like the university) labels a small local sample, how many ECGs are needed to recalibrate and re-threshold so that sensitivity is at least 95% again?
candidates.evidence: 027: the PTB-XL threshold missed 95% at SPH (JEPA 0.916, xECG 0.922) and probabilities were too high (intercept -1.1 to -1.9).
candidates.notes: Done 29 September 2026 as Experiment 029 Part A: with xECG, the pooled readout and a local Platt plus 95% threshold, no n up to 1,000 keeps sensitivity >= 0.95 in 90% of draws (0.79 at 1,000; specificity falls from 0.80 to 0.61). A pre-registered conservative order-statistic threshold does from n = 200 at SPH prevalence (about 50 positives needed) and from n = 1,000 at 5% prevalence, at specificity 0.25-0.51. 100 local ECGs fix calibration (intercept -1.6 to 0). Blending with source data fails. docs/experiment-029-local-adaptation-results.md. 1,420 s CPU for both parts.

candidates.title: Threshold stability with a larger calibration set
candidates.question: Is the 95% threshold noisy because the PTB-XL calibration set has only 564 ECGs (348 positive)?
candidates.evidence: 027 calibration set: 564 ECGs; development sensitivity was 0.930-0.951 instead of 0.95.
candidates.notes: Bootstrap the calibration set for threshold variance; compare with a cross-fitted training-set threshold. Dropped 29 September 2026: superseded by 029, which measured threshold stability against local sample size.

candidates.title: Hybrid score: supervised probe plus distance from normal
candidates.question: Does adding the one-class distance to the probe catch unseen conditions without losing overall AUROC?
candidates.evidence: 026: the distance from normal matched probes trained without a held-out condition, but trailed the full probe by 0.04-0.05.
candidates.notes: Cached 026 scores and 025 probe predictions; e.g. rank-average or a two-feature logistic fitted on training only. Value raised 29 September 2026: 029 shows a fixed sensitivity target is impractical at low prevalence; a hybrid may help most at small referral budgets. Evaluate at the budgets of referral_budget_operating_point. Done 29 September 2026 as Experiment 031 (PR #38): negative at every budget (xECG 5%: -0.028 [-0.035, -0.022]); it helps on conditions held out of the readout (MI +0.090, CD +0.085, STTC +0.068).

candidates.title: Normal manifold fitted on a small set of local normal ECGs
candidates.question: Does refitting the normal manifold on a few hundred local normal ECGs recover the SPH gap?
candidates.evidence: 026: distance from normal fell from 0.923 (PTB-XL) to 0.858 (SPH) for xECG; 027 showed calibration shifts across sites too.
candidates.notes: Done 29 September 2026 as Experiment 029 Part B: adding 50 local normals to the pooled reference beats it in 96% of draws, but the xECG gain is negligible (+0.0002 at 50, +0.003 at 1,000; reference 0.877). Recentring on the local normal mean gives +0.005-0.007 from 50-100 normals (JEPA +0.009, CPC +0.017); local-only needs about 1,000 normals to match. Best 0.883 against 0.941 for the supervised readout, so the gap does not close. docs/experiment-029-local-adaptation-results.md.

candidates.title: Label efficiency for echo-confirmed structural heart disease
candidates.question: How many echo-labeled ECGs are needed for a useful SHD readout with frozen xECG or JEPA?
candidates.evidence: 023: frozen xECG reached 0.838 with 71,823 training labels; echo labels are expensive, and PTB-XL abnormality heads reach only about 0.75.
candidates.notes: Done 29 September 2026 as Experiment 028: mean AUROC xECG/JEPA/CPC 0.752/0.734/0.728 at 100 echo labels, 0.801/0.791/0.783 at 1,000, 0.838/0.823/0.812 with all; all beat the cart head (0.737) from 250 labels; 95% of the gain over chance needs about 4,000 labels; docs/experiment-028-echo-label-efficiency-results.md. 6,655 s CPU.

candidates.title: Rerun 022 with Ningbo: do Ningbo labels improve transfer to SPH?
candidates.question: Adding Ningbo's physician labels to the PTB-XL readout: does SPH AUROC, calibration or 95%-sensitivity transfer improve?
candidates.evidence: 022/027: rankings transfer to SPH but the PTB-XL operating point does not (sensitivity about 0.92). Ningbo is a large Chinese hospital like SPH. 025: PTB-XL gains above 4,000 labels are under 0.01, so any gain should show up in transfer, not in PTB-XL development.
candidates.notes: Done 29 September 2026 as Experiment 022b (docs/experiment-022b-multisource-readout-results.md), with multisource_lso. Adding Ningbo's labeled training ECGs to the PTB-XL readout raises SPH AUROC: xECG 0.915 to 0.935 (+0.020 [+0.018, +0.022]), JEPA +0.018, CPC +0.016; Chapman/Ningbo carries half of the full multi-source gain. A threshold calibrated on PTB-XL plus Ningbo does not transfer: SPH sensitivity 0.922 to 0.841 (xECG), specificity 0.646 to 0.881. PTB-XL hard cases rank worse (0.726 to 0.687). Measured about 3 h build and 20 min CPU for both items.

candidates.title: Rerun 027 with Ningbo: calibration and threshold fitted on several hospitals
candidates.question: Does a threshold calibrated on PTB-XL plus Ningbo (and other Challenge sources) hold 95% sensitivity at SPH better than a PTB-XL-only threshold?
candidates.evidence: 027: PTB-XL-only calibration missed 95% at SPH and probabilities ran too high (intercept -1.1 to -1.9).
candidates.notes: Done 29 September 2026 as Experiment 027b (docs/experiment-027b-multisource-calibration-results.md), on the frozen Challenge record split v1 (docs/challenge-splits-v1.md). Pooled PTB-XL plus Challenge calibration is not adopted: SPH sensitivity CPC 0.971 to 0.944 (closer), JEPA 0.916 to 0.912 and xECG 0.922 to 0.920 (slightly further); no arm reaches 95% at SPH, and ECE worsens for JEPA and xECG (0.11 to 0.16-0.17). Leave-one-family-out calibration did not help a held-out hospital. Measured about 3 h build and 85 s CPU.

candidates.title: Rerun 026 with Ningbo: normal manifold fitted on normals from several hospitals
candidates.question: Does fitting the distance-from-normal score on PTB-XL plus Ningbo normals close its SPH gap?
candidates.evidence: 026: xECG distance from normal 0.923 on PTB-XL but 0.858 on SPH.
candidates.notes: Done 29 September 2026 as Experiment 026b (docs/experiment-026b-multisource-normal-manifold-results.md), on the frozen Challenge record split v1 with the training quality policy. Fitting the Mahalanobis score on PTB-XL plus 4,974 Challenge training normals (sinus rhythm alone) is adopted: SPH AUROC xECG 0.858 to 0.878 (+0.020 [+0.018, +0.022]), JEPA 0.836 to 0.865, CPC 0.791 to 0.806, about a third of the gap to the 022 probe. Chapman/Ningbo carries most of the gain; PTB-XL development falls 0.004 (xECG). Measured about 2 h build and 10 min CPU.

candidates.title: CPC continued pretraining on quality-first cohorts v2
candidates.question: Does pretraining CPC on the Ningbo-enriched quality-first cohorts narrow its gap to JEPA and xECG?
candidates.evidence: 022-026: CPC trails JEPA/xECG by about 0.035 everywhere; both were pretrained on Chapman and Ningbo, CPC was not. ECG-JEPA Table 8: more MIMIC data did not help.
candidates.notes: Lower priority now that the baseline moves to frozen JEPA/xECG. Use cohorts v3 or v4, not v2. Overlaps pretraining_scaling_curve_v3: its 50k arm answers this too.

candidates.title: Rerun 025 with Ningbo: label efficiency with PTB-XL + Ningbo labels
candidates.question: Does pooling Ningbo's labels change the label-efficiency curves or the encoder ranking, and does it help SPH?
candidates.evidence: 025: the curve is nearly flat above 4,000 labels (JEPA 0.955 to 0.959), so little change is expected on PTB-XL; this checks it.
candidates.notes: Done 29 September 2026 as Experiment 025b (docs/experiment-025b-label-efficiency-multisource-results.md): 025's draws on PTB-XL plus all Challenge training labels (22,494; Ningbo, Chapman/Shaoxing, Georgia, CPSC), drawn uniformly from the pooled pool. Decision mixed: at SPH, xECG pooled minus PTB-XL-only is +0.022 [+0.020, +0.024] at N = 250 and +0.016 [+0.015, +0.018] at N = 1,000, but only 16 and 17 of 20 draws are positive, so PTB-XL-only stays the default by the 90% rule; JEPA and CPC pass it from N = 250. 1,000 pooled labels match all 15,359 PTB-XL labels at SPH (0.915), and 100 PTB-XL labels plus every Challenge label give 0.938. Encoder ranking holds. Pooling costs 0.008 on ordinary PTB-XL development and about 0.05 on the hard added subset (xECG). Measured about 2.5 h build and 35 min CPU.

candidates.title: Why pooled readouts lose on the PTB-XL hard added subset
candidates.question: Why do readouts fitted on PTB-XL plus the Challenge sources lose about 0.07 AUROC on 022's hard added PTB-XL development subset (022b), and which change to the Challenge labels or inputs removes the loss?
candidates.evidence: 022b: pooled minus PTB-XL-only on the added subset (266 ECGs, 41 positive) is -0.072 [-0.113, -0.032] for xECG against -0.005 on ordinary development; 025b: -0.053 at N = all. 025b also shows the subset depends on having its training analogues: without the 1,724 PTB-XL training ECGs the project label dropped, xECG PTB-XL-only falls from 0.726 to 0.615.
candidates.notes: Candidate causes: label-definition differences between the PTB-XL superclasses and the Challenge SNOMED mapping (IRBBB 713426002 and other CD form codes counted positive, rhythm or form codes, the sinus-rhythm-alone negative); and device or filter shift between PTB-XL and the Challenge sources. Arms: drop or relabel Challenge rows by code group, and a device or high-pass control (see highpass_ablation, device_control). Score the 1,724 dropped PTB-XL training ECGs by cross-fitting as a larger analogue, since the development subset has 41 positives. Overlaps hard_case_analysis. Done 30 September 2026 as Experiment 035 (PR #45): the hard subset is NORM-plus-minor-code ECGs that the Challenge mapping never calls negative; reweighting PTB-XL's 1,724 analogues (dropped_upweighted) recovers 81% of the loss with no SPH cost.

candidates.title: Rerun 024 with Ningbo: embedding geometry across sources

candidates.notes: Done 29 September 2026 as Experiment 024b (docs/experiment-024b-multisource-geometry-results.md): k-means on a balanced draw of 4,356 training ECGs per family (PTB-XL, Chapman/Ningbo, Georgia, CPSC). Clusters follow the diagnosis more than the hospital: xECG k = 8 family AMI 0.047 against label AMI 0.125, difference -0.078 [-0.084, -0.072]; all 36 robustness contrasts below 0 (CPC gaps small, at most 0.025). 024's device-over-diagnosis pattern is CPC-only; JEPA and xECG follow the label within PTB-XL too. Hospital is still linearly encoded (source-family probe mean AUROC 0.925-0.949) and enriches neighbors (41-58% own family against 25%); kNN without same-family neighbors loses 0.012-0.099 AUROC. At SPH, pooled-label prototypes trail the probe by 0.044 (xECG), 0.043 (JEPA), 0.099 (CPC); pooling narrows the gap. MI medoids are still all CS100 3 PTB-XL ECGs. 024 and 022b reproduced exactly. Measured about 2 h build and 33 min CPU.

candidates.title: Operating point set by referral budget, fitted on local normals only
candidates.question: If the threshold is set so a fixed share of normal ECGs is referred (2%, 5%, 10%), how many local normal ECGs fix it, and what sensitivity does each readout reach at SPH and in each Challenge family?
candidates.evidence: 029: a guaranteed 95% sensitivity needs at least 45 local positives and then refers 49-75% of normals; at 5% prevalence it refers about 800 per 1,000. A referral-rate threshold is a quantile of normal scores, which a mostly healthy student pilot supplies.
candidates.notes: Done 29 September 2026 as Experiment 030: with the pooled xECG readout, a threshold at the 95th percentile of local normals holds a 5% budget within +/-1 pp in 89% of draws at 1,000 normals and 96% at 2,000 (52% at 200), so (A) is not reached by 1,000. Pooled beats PTB-XL-only by +0.084 and the distance score by +0.186 at 5%. docs/experiment-030-referral-budget-results.md. 6 s CPU plus about 2.5 build hours.
